record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: For every space bound S(n) with S(n) at least log n, is the class DSPACE(S(n)) of languages accepted by deterministic Turing machines using O(S(n)) work tape space equal to the class NSPACE(S(n)) accepted by nondeterministic Turing machines using O(S(n)) work tape space? In particular, does this hold in the special case S(n)=n, the linear-bounded-automaton (LBA) case?

evidence.quote: 1. Is DSPACE(S(n)) = NSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) >_ logn ?2 The special case S(n) = n is called "the LBA problem" and has been studied for over ten years

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a function $S:\mathbb{N}	o\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{DSPACE}(S(n))$ denote the class of languages $L\subseteq\Sigma^*$ accepted by some deterministic Turing machine with a read-only input tape and a separate work tape such that, on every input of length $n$, the machine uses $O(S(n))$ cells on the work tape. Let $\mathrm{NSPACE}(S(n))$ denote the analogous class defined using nondeterministic Turing machines with the same $O(S(n))$ work-tape bound.

Question: Is it true that for every space-constructible function $S(n)$ with $S(n) \geq \log n$, one has
$$\mathrm{DSPACE}(S(n)) \;=\; \mathrm{NSPACE}(S(n))?$$
In particular, in the special case $S(n) = n$ (the linear-bounded automaton, or LBA, problem), does $\mathrm{DSPACE}(n) = \mathrm{NSPACE}(n)$ hold?
artifact.status_search_result: The LBA problem (whether DSPACE(n) = NSPACE(n)) and the more general question of whether DSPACE(S(n)) = NSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) ≥ log n remain longstanding open problems in complexity theory. Savitch's theorem gives NSPACE(S) ⊆ DSPACE(S^2), and the Immerman–Szelepcsényi theorem (1987–88) shows NSPACE(S) is closed under complement, but equality with DSPACE(S) is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: LBA problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The LBA problem asks whether the set of languages recognized by nondeterministic LBAs equals the set recognized by deterministic LBAs. This problem has been open since 1964.
status_evidence.claim: The deterministic vs nondeterministic linear space (LBA) problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Savitch's theorem / Immerman–Szelepcsényi
status_evidence.snippet: NSPACE(S) is closed under complement for S(n) ≥ log n; equality with DSPACE(S) remains open.
status_evidence.claim: DSPACE(S(n)) = NSPACE(S(n)) is still an open question for S(n) ≥ log n.
